zotero.abstractNote: Single-cell RNA-seq data without unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are characterized by overdispersion and a high frequency of zero counts. While Pearson residuals are widely used for normalization and dimensionality reduction of UMI-based data, they are not directly applicable to non-UMI data. We propose a compound model approach to calculate Pearson residuals for non-UMI data, accounting for both the biological variability and the technical noise inherent in these protocols. We demonstrate that our method outperforms existing approaches in terms of capturing biological signal and reducing technical batch effects.
